g.text: CLI flow — find-target, the IPv6 split, and the reachability method tree (numbered)
— netboot server · START FIRST, leave RUNNING
(find-target PRINTS this when no cabled target is seen yet)
[2] MAC … · IP 192.168.1.x — pick the MAC on the TARGET's screen
auto-detect: does THIS host have working IPv6?
(OPTIONAL — only if a 1.Y IPv6 method was chosen AND [Q2] = 0c/0d, a different network)
ARE YOU SURE THE TARGET WILL HAVE IPV6?
(the box ALSO re-checks after boot — prints
if a v6-only method has none; req 167)
— how the box gets online AFTER install:
cable → R + wifi → B (a DIFFERENT router)
— type the box LAN IP; added the 5 DNS records? (port-forward only)
⚠ router / DIRECT IPv6 — AAAA → box IPv6 (open firewall, NO relay)
⚠ DuckDNS + IPv6 — AAAA → box IPv6 (free name, NO relay)
relays: Cloudflare / ngrok / pinggy / localtunnel (outbound; v6 or v4)
sub: per relay — domain / token (see B.* in req 166)
⚠ router port-forward :443 (needs PUBLIC IPv4, NOT CGNAT — auto-checked)
relays: Cloudflare / ngrok / pinggy / localtunnel (outbound IPv4)
boot it in UEFI network mode → it shows its
the INPUT you give / a check

Numbered for precise edits ("edit 1.Y.B"). ⚠ = fully-sovereign (no relay) or a caution. Tree-leaf inputs are inline (separate input boxes only for the linear steps, to stay readable). Default = 1.*.B/C Tailscale.
